learningObjective: Distinguish correct claims about RMSNorm's compute pattern from common overgeneralizations.

canonicalClaims.claim: RMSNorm is memory-bandwidth bound: HBM traffic (read x, read weight, write y) dominates; the reduction and rsqrt are negligible in wall-clock cost on modern GPUs.
conditions: Row length fits typical hardware tile; extreme long rows require online algorithms.
FP32 accumulation is used for stability.
nonImplications: Does not imply the reduction cost is exactly zero; on very short rows it can matter.
Does not imply RMSNorm and LayerNorm are numerically equivalent.

misconceptions.claim: RMSNorm is compute-bound because it uses rsqrt.
misconceptions.whyWrong: rsqrt is a single cheap instruction per row; HBM traffic dominates.

misconceptions.claim: RMSNorm equals LayerNorm on zero-mean inputs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They differ in bias term and in whether mean is subtracted; parameterizations differ.
Only sum(x^2) is needed; mean of x is not used.

implementationFacts: Row-parallel Triton RMSNorm kernels typically use BLOCK == row length for a single-pass reduction.
For rows exceeding on-chip capacity, an online (two-pass) variant is used.
performanceScenarios: RMSNorm is commonly fused with the previous residual add and the next linear projection input read.
